title: Mall Mein Ek Dukaan Ka Rent Kitna Hota Hai? Mall Owner Kaise Kamata Hai?
description: The 'har pump pe mart, tyre shop aur car wash kyun' payoff in the ₹17 crore pump reel pulled 1.8M views. Our multiplex and banquet reels covered one tenant type but not the mall owner's model.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: HOW A MALL EARNS (India, data to Nov 2026)

HOW TO READ THIS
- ✅ = figure taken directly from a source.
- 🧮 = simple arithmetic I did on sourced figures. The inputs are sourced, but the result is my calculation.
- ⚠️ = estimate, blog/consultant figure, or conflicting data. Verify before it goes on screen.
- Rents are quoted per sq ft per month on chargeable area, not carpet area.

---

**0. THE HOOK CHECK**
- Rent for 1,000 sq ft, using sourced per sq ft rates (🧮):
  - ₹200–250/sq ft (Bengaluru Grade A/A+ average) = ₹2,00,000–₹2,50,000 a month. The average mall rental in Bengaluru is ~₹200–250 per sq ft (chargeable, vanilla stores). [https://websitemedia.anarock.com/media/Leasing_Trends_in_Malls_Across_Top_Metropolitan_Cities_c0d6925658_e626f1b237.pdf]
  - ₹346/sq ft (current mall average, vanilla) = ₹3,46,000 a month. Vanilla stores average ~INR 346 psf; kiosks are ~INR 618 psf. [same Anarock May 2026 PDF]
  - ₹400–450/sq ft (Mumbai region) = ₹4,00,000–₹4,50,000 a month. The MMR average is ~₹400-450 per sq ft (chargeable). [same Anarock PDF]
- ⚠️ I found no sourced car-EMI figure. The scriptwriter needs one before the "Gaadi ki EMI" line goes out. By these numbers, rent is likely a multiple of a typical car EMI, not just "more than".

---

**1. THREE WAYS A TENANT PAYS (fixed vs revenue share)**
- Fixed rent is a pre-set rate per sq ft, and sales don't change it. Tenants pay a pre-set rent every month, calculated per square foot, and sales performance doesn't influence it. [https://www.orionmalls.com/blogs/retail-leasing-models-fixed-rent-vs-revenue-sharing]
- Pure revenue share means rent is a percentage of the tenant's sales. It is often 6-12% of gross monthly revenue, with or without a minimum guarantee. [same Orion link]
- Hybrid is the norm. ~74.2% of deals are structured as Rental + Revenue Share. Pure revenue share or pure rent models remain minimal across categories. [https://websitemedia.anarock.com/media/Leasing_Trends_in_Malls_Across_Top_Metropolitan_Cities_c0d6925658_e626f1b237.pdf]
- Nexus Select Trust is India's listed retail REIT. It reports in-place rent as the higher of the minimum guaranteed rent or the revenue share. [https://www.nexusselecttrust.com/resources/assets/pdf/Nexus-Select-Trust-Jun-26-v12.pdf]
- Nexus's turnover rent is the contracted % of tenant sales, less the minimum guaranteed rent for the same period, or nil. [same Nexus Q1 FY27 deck]
- Nexus turnover-rent percentages typically range from 5-25% of tenant sales, subject to a minimum guaranteed threshold. [https://www.samco.in/ipo/nexus-select-trust-reit-ipo]
